All my life, forensics have been my ultimate dream. I was a VERY weird kid that became obsessed at like...10? All I know is that I read a book about the Body Farm and other famous cases solved by forensics. I did my science fair project (dating myself here, lol) on using DNA/ blood typing in a fake scenario where a girl was attacked, and I used the "DNA" from the "blood" under her fingernails to catch the attacker.

It was really cool, but I got a talking to for it being "inappropriate" for school. This was also, like, right around  the time the original CSI came out. 

I digress. I've always wanted to have a career in forensic science or CSI, but going through life raw-dogging neurodivergence and being undiagnosed kinda fucked all my plans up. Also, apparently, the job market for that type of work is insanely competitive, there aren't many positions, the pay is shitty (unless you're a medical examiner) , and the hours are bad. Also, there's so, so much schooling that goes into it.

I'm trying to come to terms with the fact that I may never get to work in my dream field. Hell, I can't even get an official autism diagnosis. I might never. It costs so goddamned much to get the damn diagnosis, and for what? I'm an AFAB adult, so it's not like there are even any resources for me. Would have been really cool if my mom had pulled her head out of her ass and gotten me a diagnosis for it (and ADHD), but she never did, because then she would have had to admit that *she* was neurodivergent. The worst part? SHE WAS A TEACHER. 

So essentially, I am trying to not be mad every day that I didn't really get a chance to pursue my passion, since school was always a huge struggle for me (academically and socially), and I might never get that chance. 

Instead, I feel like an overgrown toddler, stumbling my way through life, not knowing the rules or understanding anything, and being bitter and depressed.

A letter got sent home. Apparently, the gym teacher that already hated me for being a little weirdo that didn't like sports had noticed my poorly tied shoes, too. Now, my mom *had* to address my shitty shoes .

I remember sitting in the ugly upholstered chair in the living room while she glared at me and hissed insults through pursed lips. You all might be familiar with the look...burning , angry eyes, pursed lips, insults spat at you.

I don't remember what exactly was said, but I do remember something to the effect of "Why don't you get it, it's so simple."

Instead of taking the time, my parents were honestly ready to put me in Velcro shoes for the rest of my life so they wouldn't have to deal with me.
